title: Validate readinto buffers before consuming input and count bytes, not elements
applies_when: A Python file-like wrapper implements readinto with len(buffer), reads first, or assigns bytes directly to an array or typed/multidimensional memoryview.
lesson: Resolve the actual buffer protocol before reading: a typed view's len counts elements (or its first dimension), not byte capacity, and direct slice assignment can reject bytes after the stream position has already advanced. For a byte-oriented readinto contract, acquire a new memoryview, reject read-only destinations and form a writable C-contiguous byte view before consuming input. Read at most that byte view's length and return bytes transferred. Release only temporary views, not the caller's object. Pair bytearray, integer array, typed/shaped/sliced memoryview and empty-buffer cases with native FileIO; also test read-only, noncontiguous and non-buffer inputs at interior positions and EOF, asserting failure leaves the position and remaining input unchanged. Ordinary bytearray-only tests miss the typed-length and late-validation failures.
avoid_when: A protocol that explicitly supports strided scatter or element-oriented transfers needs its own contract; nbytes alone does not establish contiguity or writability. Check combined-error precedence separately: fsspec's existing closed-file ValueError can be retained by read(0), while closed BytesIO with a readonly target raises TypeError on the observed Linux3.12/Windows3.14 runtimes. Neither priority is a Python-wide requirement; deliberately changing it is a compatibility decision. This change is not zero-copy I/O, thread-safety or performance evidence. JuiceFS evidence covers native Linux Python3.12.13 with current-source Go1.25.10 libjfs, SQLite and local object storage, not the full service CI matrix. Peer validation and retrieval do not prove maintainer acceptance, Scout conversion improvement or prospective evidence-selection utility.

evidence.note: Another author's PR2260 head guards the already-cast memoryview before reading. This is a PR revision, not a merged-main fix. Independent Windows3.14 runs of the author's 50 registered regressions give baseline36 failures/14 controls and head50 pass; removing only read(0) changes the two closed-file expectations. Linux real-package stdlib controls omit NumPy and pytest collection; a separate controller check incorrectly expected BytesIO to raise ValueError and was retained as a failed premise.

Published peer verification separates the documented readonly attribute, the concrete late-validation defect, and the wrapper-specific exception-precedence decision. No competing PR or whole-suite/CI qualification.
The byte-oriented API requires a writable bytes-like destination and returns bytes read. The documentation is an API contract, not a measurement of a third-party wrapper.
A byte cast creates a new view without copying the buffer and is restricted by contiguity; the adjacent nbytes examples distinguish byte capacity from element count and multidimensional len.
Current-main reproduction: typed arrays fail after consuming input; invalid destinations can advance position or be accepted at EOF. No mock libjfs was used.

Two-file repair with native before/after buffer checks, 330 raw/buffered FileIO differential cases and 64 existing stream regressions. First CI exposed inherited test-fixture collisions missed by the isolated base-class run; dedicated ReadintoTests plus 46 selected native SDK cases verify the test-placement correction. Source/test bytes match committed Git blobs. Submitted Ready, not an accepted merge or full service-backend matrix result.
